subject: questions about results from the adegenet server

messages.author: e251dfe1bb017bb7
messages.subject: questions about results from the adegenet server
parts:
Hi-
Basically, this set of questions are:  why did the adegenetServer give me different results than running dapc() itself? .

First: how I did the analysis:
I have been looking at the number of subpopulations in my bird data set: 64 individuals, 3529 SNPs.  I had lots more SNPs but removed all those that had any missing data.

I ran find.clusters() retaining 30 to 60 pcs in 5 pc steps, using both the kmeans and the ward clustering methods.  Ward seemed to work better, but both methods gave 4 groups when 35 or 40 pcs were retained and they seemed reasonable.

When I ran dapc() I always put in for n.pca the number of pcs I had retained in the find.clusters step (40 in this case).
QUESTION1:  Is that the right choice n.pca for the dapc computation?
QUESTION2:  the number of discriminant function eigenvalues had two of the eigenvalues much larger than the 3d, so I kept only 2.  IS that right, or should I have kept all 3?

When I then looked at the posterior membership probabilities, for the particular run I am concerned about I saw that group members of 2 of the 4 groups had 100% membership probability---that's fine.  For members of the other 2 groups they had membership probabilities partly in one group and partly in the other---no problem. 
Running assignplot seemed to agree with memberships.

Here is where I have the big question: I don't seem to get the same results when I run the adegenet server:

I executed: adegenetServer(what=c("DAPC"))
and looked at the compoplot.  ****When I put in 40 for the "number of PCA axes retained", I got a plot with 100% group membership for each of individuals for each of the 4 groups!  *** Not partial memberships for those in the 2 mixed groups.*** 
However, when I instead checked the box for "Use suggested number of PCA components" ***I got the correct 100% memberships when I should have and partial memberships for the others---just like posterior membership probabilities!*** But the "suggested number of PCAs" was only 5, not 40!  And when I ran cross validation with 100 steps, the value of 40 came out as the right one to use.
QUESTION3:  why didn't using 40 for the compoplot calculation work?

QUESTION4: If I say that I used 3 (all) of the DA axes instead of 2, the plot changed.  Here's why I wonder if I should always use all of the discriminants rather than ignoring the 3d small one.

Thank you very much! DAPC appears to be just what I need for my analysis, but getting different results with the adegenetServer makes me question what's right and what's wrong.

Regards

Janice Boyd
Texas A&M University
